reasons: No test is visible in the packet.
Missing and editorial states are shown explicitly.

terms.meaning: One item on the scan screen, such as a line of text or a figure.
A number calculated from other numbers, which has its own inputs.
A label for the current condition of an item.

sections.name: File setup, SourceState
sections.title: Imports and design notes
sections.what: Brings in icons and the types for scan elements, citations and full citation targets. A comment explains that the sources view reuses the shared drawer and never invents support.
sections.why: The comment records the intent behind the file.

sections.name: elementRefs
sections.title: Collecting the references
sections.what: Returns the list of references for one element, using the list when present or the single source otherwise.
sections.why: Likely reason: supports both the newer list format and the older single source.

sections.name: isCitable
sections.title: Is a reference provable
sections.what: Says yes when a reference has an evidence id or a quote.
sections.why: The comment says a field pointer alone is not proof.
sections.watch_out: A quote alone counts as provable, even if it is not registered as evidence.

sections.name: elementSourceState
sections.title: Deciding the source status
sections.what: Labels the element as cited, stored, editorial or missing. Text containing a number with no source is marked missing.
sections.why: Likely reason: makes gaps in support visible.
sections.watch_out: The number rule can mark labels with digits as missing unless a state is set on the element.

sections.name: openRef
sections.title: Choosing the citation view
sections.what: Opens the matching view: stored research quotes directly, registered research and project evidence through the full lookup, or a plain citation otherwise.
sections.why: Likely reason: each source type stores its data differently.
sections.watch_out: Routing depends on the id prefix and which fields exist, so a new reference type falls into the plain path.

sections.name: RefRow
sections.title: One reference row
sections.what: Shows the title, a status tag when not fetched, a Full quote or Check evidence button, an Original link, the quote, notes, the derived formula and nested inputs.
sections.why: Shows each source with what is known and what is not.
sections.watch_out: Nested inputs are shown recursively, and the code sets no depth limit.

sections.name: SourceRefList
sections.title: Sources section
sections.what: Builds the Sources box: the editorial or missing notice when it applies, then the list of references.
sections.why: Likely reason: one place for each element's sources.
sections.watch_out: The notices only appear for their states, so a stored element may show no notice at all.

summary: Shows the Sources area for one scan element: each reference with its quote and a button to open the full citation, or a note explaining why there is no source.
purpose: Lets readers check where each claim came from.
why: The code comment says it is the one sources view for each element and never invents support.
how: Works out a state for the element: cited, stored, editorial or missing. Lists its references, including nested inputs for derived values. Each reference opens the matching citation view depending on its type.
inputs: One scan element, a handler for full citations, and a handler for plain citations.
outputs: A sources section with buttons, quotes and links.
risks: Reference ids starting with rs are handled specially, so changing that prefix breaks lookups. Any text containing a number and no source is marked missing, which can flag harmless text.
debug: If an element shows missing, check its sources and quote fields. If a button does nothing, check the id prefix and the handlers passed in.
